note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 159, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

The U.S. infantry component receives a representative forage-cap and muzzle-loading long-arm analogy. This is not an exact uniform or firing-mechanism reconstruction. The Mexican infantry component receives the separate reviewed assignment below; no common uniform is inferred for both armies. Equipment sources do not replace the separate CDB personnel estimates.

The US Army Center of Military History identifies Mexican line and light infantry, active militia, cavalry and artillery in Santa Anna's army (CMH 73-4, pp.17–18). Its account also notes shortages of heavy coats and shoes during the winter march (p.13). A shako and Brown Bess figure represents one equipped infantry component of the mixed Mexican force. The blue/red tailcoat and light canvas trousers are a documented war-period clothing analogy; the sources do not establish that every unit or soldier wore this combination at this battle. Regiment, season, supply, militia dress and weapons varied. No infantry proportion, additional force, strength, loss or death count is inferred. In particular, this figure does not establish universal summer dress during the cold February battle.
